candidates.attacker_control: The caller controls the REST query parameters handle, sequence and filename of /api/core/bitstreams/search/byItemHandle. Handles are institutional identifiers that are frequently public (and enumerable/guessable via item listings and OAI/other public endpoints). No authentication or CSRF-protected state change is needed: the method carries no @PreAuthorize, so the DSpace method-security layer imposes no check and the web filter chain deliberately permitAll()s /api/** (WebSecurityConfiguration).
candidates.counterevidence_checked: Verified that BitstreamRestController.retrieve still enforces READ before streaming content (BitstreamServiceImpl.retrieve -> authorizeService.authorizeAction(...,READ)), so this is not a file-content bypass. Verified that DSpaceObjectConverter/BitstreamConverter add no authorization. Checked that RestResourceController and DSpaceRestRepository.add no implicit authentication requirement for search methods (only explicit @PreAuthorize annotations apply; other DSpace search methods such as EPersonRestRepository.findByMetadata do carry explicit annotations, this one does not). Checked that for public item+bundle combinations METADATA_READ would be granted by BitstreamMetadataReadPermissionEvaluatorPlugin anyway (READ on item and bundle), which limits the observable delta to non-readable items/bundles (withdrawn/restricted material), and checked that no other code path in the module re-applies the check for this method. Could not diff this file against upstream DSpace to prove the check was present and removed - the javadoc statement plus the unused @Autowired AuthorizeService field are the internal evidence for removal.
candidates.impact: Information disclosure of restricted-file metadata: file names, sizes, checksum values (MD5/SHA), bundle and format information, bitstream UUIDs, sequence numbers and the derived /content URL of bitstreams in items/bundles the requester is not allowed to read (e.g. restricted/embargoed resources, withdrawn items reachable via their public handle). Checksums and exact names can be used to confirm the identity of known files and to map a repository's hidden holdings; it also makes restricted items' file inventories enumerable without any account. Integrity of the stored content is not directly affected.
candidates.prerequisites: Anonymous or any authenticated user who can reach /api/**; a known/guessed item handle; for the exposure to be meaningful the targeted bitstream must be one for which the caller lacks METADATA_READ - i.e. a file in a non-readable item/bundle (e.g. restricted/embargoed items, or withdrawn items that retain a public handle). Content download itself remains gated by READ in BitstreamRestController/BitstreamServiceImpl.retrieve, so exposure is limited to bitstream metadata.
candidates.root_cause: BitstreamRestRepository.findByItemHandle (dspace-server-webapp, exposed as /api/core/bitstreams/search/byItemHandle) resolves an Item from a caller-supplied handle and then collects all Bitstreams of all Bundles via item.getBundles()/bundle.getBitstreams() and returns converter.toRest(matchedBitstream,...) without any authorization check. The method has no @PreAuthorize and performs no in-body permission check, even though its javadoc explicitly promises the check ('will be returned if the user has "METADATA_READ" access') and the class declares an @Autowired AuthorizeService field that is unused anywhere in the file - the exact leftover expected if the documented check was removed. Compare findOne (line 92: hasPermission(#id,'BITSTREAM','METADATA_READ')) and the BitstreamFormat/accessStatus link repositories, which all enforce METADATA_READ, and BitstreamMetadataReadPermissionEvaluatorPlugin which defines exactly the semantics (admin, or READ on bitstream, or READ on parent item AND first bundle).
candidates.title: Missing METADATA_READ authorization in REST search method BitstreamRestRepository.findByItemHandle (bitstream metadata disclosure)
candidates.trace: GET /api/core/bitstreams/search/byItemHandle?handle=<handle>&sequence=<n> (or &filename=<name>) -> RestResourceController search dispatch invokes BitstreamRestRepository.findByItemHandle (no @PreAuthorize, BitstreamRestRepository.java:170-197) -> handleService.resolveToObject(context, handle) performs no authorization (HandleServiceImpl.java:242-255) -> getFirstMatchedBitstream walks item.getBundles() then bundle.getBitstreams() and returns the first match by sequenceId or name without any authorizeService call (lines 199-219) -> converter.toRest(matchedBitstream, ...) serializes BitstreamRest with id, name, bundleName, sizeBytes, checksum (algorithm+value), sequenceId, bitstream metadata and the content link (BitstreamConverter.java:30-48, BitstreamRest.java:34-72) -> HTTP 200 to a caller who has neither READ nor METADATA_READ on that bitstream. The class's only permission-related member, the @Autowired AuthorizeService (lines 67-68), is never referenced in the file, and the javadoc at line 162 documents the check that the code does not perform.
candidates.unverified: No runtime execution was performed (no tests/scanners). Exploitability (HTTP status of the search endpoint for an anonymous caller, exact DSpace version behaviour of the search dispatch, and which metadata fields are serialized for a restricted bitstream) is argued only from source. Whether upstream DSpace contains the removed check could not be confirmed because no network access or sibling-condition/patch data is available; the finding therefore remains a lead, not a confirmed vulnerability.
candidates.weakness_type: CWE-862 Missing Authorization (metadata disclosure; CWE-200 information exposure)

coverage_summary: Source-only review of the assigned DSpace 9.1-SNAPSHOT tree (3415 readable files; 0 binary/oversize/symlink exclusions). Using get_source_scope and get_relation_scope I accounted for: the P1 index is a partial syntactic index (3356 of 3415 files indexed, 59 source files missing, 632 files parsed, no control-flow/data-flow/semantic resolution, no runtime reachability, no SAST oracle); all index edges/labels were treated as navigation hints only and every candidate edge used was verified in source text. I examined request-facing code in dspace-server-webapp (REST repositories, controllers, security filters/JWT/CSRF/permission-evaluator plugins, submission and workflow paths, bitstream download/metadata paths, OIDC/SAML/Shibboleth/ORCID login filters, sitemap, signposting/IIIF/OAI entry points), dspace-api (AuthorizeServiceImpl, Bitstream/WorkspaceItem/Item/Collection/Community services, EPerson/Account/PasswordHash, requestitem/access-token flow, LDN/COAR Notify, ORCID/DOI/Sherpa/OpenAIRE clients, curation tasks, packagers/METS, bitstore path handling, discovery/Solr query builders and browse DAO, statistics) and the servlet/security code of dspace-oai, dspace-sword(v2), dspace-rdf, dspace-saml2. Areas inspected more shallowly (sampled rather than fully read): the many CLI/admin scripts and curate tasks in dspace-api, the bulk-import/export and metadata import/export implementations, statistics utilities, and parts of the sword/swordv2 and iiif modules.
limitations: No execution: no builds, tests, scanners or exploit payloads were run; nothing is runtime-confirmed and all impact statements are source-based reasoning.

I could not diff the snapshot against upstream DSpace (no network, no git history, no sibling conditions/patch data), so I cannot prove that the missing check in findByItemHandle was removed rather than never present; the javadoc's explicit METADATA_READ promise, the unused @Autowired AuthorizeService field, and the consistent METADATA_READ enforcement on sibling bitstream paths are the supporting internal evidence.

The P1 relation index is partial (59 source files not indexed, no data-flow/control-flow or semantic resolution, ~53k unresolved calls); its categories ('security_call', 'guard', etc.) are syntax-name hints only and were not treated as findings.
src/test trees are absent from the snapshot, so I could not use tests to corroborate intended authorization behaviour.
Large parts of the dspace-api CLI/script surface and the sword/swordv2/iiif modules were only sampled; a different high-impact issue there cannot be excluded.

Configuration-dependent behaviour (e.g. DSpace deployments where bundle/item READ implies METADATA_READ vs. restricted items) was evaluated only from source; the practical severity for a given deployment was not measured.

rejected_leads.lead: POST /api/workflow/workflowitems (WorkflowItemRestRepository.createAndReturn(Context,List<String>), dspace-server-webapp/.../repository/WorkflowItemRestRepository.java:164-186) has no @PreAuthorize and SubmissionService.createWorkflowItem (dspace-server-webapp/.../submit/SubmissionService.java:246-283) parses a workspace-item id out of the request body, finds it without authorization (WorkspaceItemServiceImpl.find performs no check) and calls workflowService.start, which moves the in-progress item into the workflow / can archive it (XmlWorkflowServiceImpl.java:201-241).
rejected_leads.reason: Genuine-looking missing ownership check and high potential impact, but I could not establish that a check belongs here: sibling uri-list create methods (e.g. OrcidHistoryRestRepository) do carry annotations, yet the base DSpaceRestRepository.createAndReturn(Context,List) has none and no leftover import/field indicates a deleted check, so this is at least as likely to be long-standing upstream behaviour rather than the review case. Kept as an unconfirmed lead only, since the output allows one candidate.

rejected_leads.lead: BitstreamRestController.retrieve pre-authorization is relaxed to "#accessToken != null || hasPermission(#uuid,'BITSTREAM','READ')" (lines 120-157) while token validation is skipped when requestACopyEnabled() is false (lines 325-331), and that method's comment ('If the feature is not enabled, throw exception') does not match its implementation.
rejected_leads.reason: I traced the whole path: when the token is not validated, the response resource is the plain BitstreamResource, which does not disable the authorization system and whose fetchDocument() calls bitstreamService.retrieve -> authorizeService.authorizeAction(...,READ), so no unrestricted download was demonstrated; the mismatch remains a code-quality/inconsistency lead, not an evidence-backed vulnerability.

rejected_leads.lead: Solr/Browse query construction concatenates request parameters without escaping: SolrBrowseDAO.getSolrResponse uses "{!field f=" + facetField + ... + value/authority (dspace-api/.../browse/SolrBrowseDAO.java:216-223) with values taken raw from request parameters in BrowseItemLinkRepository/BrowseEntryLinkRepository (filterValue, filterAuthority), and DSpaceItemSolrRepository builds new SolrQuery("item.handle:" + parts[2]) from the OAI identifier (dspace-oai/.../DSpaceItemSolrRepository.java:59-63).
rejected_leads.reason: Escaping is applied for other parameters in the same method (startsWith via ClientUtils.escapeQueryChars) and elsewhere in the code base; the unescaped concatenations look like long-standing upstream code, and the {!field f=...} local-params form plus surrounding default filter queries make a concrete injection impact unproven. Not selected as the single candidate.

rejected_leads.lead: Weak non-cryptographic randomness for security tokens: Utils.generateBytesKey (dspace-api/.../core/Utils.java:196-203) mixes java.util.Random bytes with VMID/timestamp/counter and MD5; it feeds generateHexKey(), used for account registration / password-reset tokens (AccountServiceImpl.java:524), request-a-copy tokens and request-a-copy access tokens (RequestItemServiceImpl.java:105,153).
rejected_leads.reason: Real weakness (CWE-330/338) but it is the long-standing DSpace design, and predicting a token also requires the per-JVM VMID, so no concrete exploitability was established. Left as an unverified lead.

summary: Reviewed the DSpace 9.1-SNAPSHOT source tree (3415 files; Java modules dspace-api, dspace-server-webapp, dspace-oai, dspace-sword, dspace-swordv2, dspace-iiif, dspace-rdf, dspace-saml2, dspace-services/statistics). I traced request-facing input from anonymous/low-privilege REST and servlet entry points into service and DAO layers, focusing on authorization checks, redirects, XML parsing, Solr/browse query construction, file/zip handling, token/key generation and authentication filters. Most candidate sinks turned out to be protected by a second enforcement layer or by upstream hardening (details in rejected_leads). The strongest single issue is a missing authorization check on the REST search method BitstreamRestRepository.findByItemHandle: the method's own javadoc states bitstream metadata is returned only "if the user has METADATA_READ access", the class autowires AuthorizeService but never uses it, and the look-up path walks items/bundles/bitstreams without invoking any authorization service, unlike the sibling findOne path which enforces hasPermission(..., 'BITSTREAM', 'METADATA_READ').
